claim: For every finite nonempty edge-transitive simple graph \(H=(V,E)\), put \(G=\mathbb F_2^V\), \(\Omega_H=\{0\}\cup\{e_u+e_v:uv\in E\}\), \(m=|E|\), and \(M=\operatorname{MAXCUT}(H)\). Then the Turán extremum \(\tau(H)=\sup\{\sum_{x\in G}f(x):f(0)=1,\ f\text{ positive definite},\ \operatorname{supp}f\subseteq\Omega_H\}\) satisfies \(\tau(H)=2M/(2M-m)=\chi_q(H)\), where \(\chi_q\) is Šámal's cubical chromatic number. A sharp extremizer is given by \(f(0)=1\) and \(f(e_u+e_v)=1/(2M-m)\) on every edge. For every odd cycle \(H=C_{2k+1}\), this normalized extremizer is unique and \(\tau(C_{2k+1})=4k/(2k-1)\).

correctness.rationale: On \(\mathbb F_2^V\), positive definiteness makes the edge coefficients real and is equivalent to nonnegative Fourier values. Each Fourier inequality is exactly a cut inequality \(1+W-2a(C)\ge0\). Averaging a maximum cut over automorphisms is valid because edge transitivity gives incidence frequency \(M/m\), yielding the sharp upper bound. The uniform edge coefficient \(1/(2M-m)\) has Fourier minimum zero exactly at maximum cuts. Odd-cycle uniqueness follows because every maximum cut omits one edge, forcing all edge coefficients equal. All hypotheses, quantifiers, and the strict positivity \(2M-m>0\) are accounted for.

value.rationale: The result is a structural infinite-family theorem rather than a finite recomputation: it identifies a harmonic Turán invariant with cubical chromatic number for every finite nonempty edge-transitive graph. This transfers exact maximum-cut information to positive-definite extremal functions, supplies an explicit universal extremizer, and gives a complete uniqueness statement for odd cycles. The bridge is reusable across symmetric graph families and is not motivated by an arbitrary numerical slice.
